hero.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor's wife of running anonymous accounts attacking Governor
hero.body:
Several social media accounts were shut down after prominent members of Ron DeSantis' administration alleged that Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, operated anonymous profiles used to criticize the governor. Christina Pushaw, a Communications Specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, both presented evidence they said connected the accounts to the Second Lady. The accounts were deactivated shortly after the accusations became public.

Pushaw shared information from Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing that the account @FSUdude01670 appeared linked to a phone number and email address similar to those known to belong to Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots from two-factor authentication attempts that displayed partial information for both an email address and phone number. Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, which she claimed was tied to Layla Collins. According to Pushaw's posts, the account content focused exclusively on promoting Jay Collins and attacking those who did not endorse him, including the governor himself. Redfern confirmed the connection, stating that the FSUDude account was directly tied to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number.

The controversy has intensified during an already contentious gubernatorial race. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year, and he subsequently appointed Layla Collins to the state Board of Education. Both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretary for DeSantis. Redfern currently works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for governor. Meanwhile, Collins is struggling in the race, having raised only about $15,500 in hard money during the week through June 26 and holding less than $3.5 million total as of that date. Donalds has consolidated endorsements from major state officials including Attorney General James Uthmeier, Agriculture Secretary Wilton Simpson, and incoming Florida Senate President Jim Boyd.

Collins has not publicly responded to the allegations about his wife's social media accounts. Florida Politics requested comment from both Jay and Layla Collins but had not received a response as of publication. The incident adds significant complexity to DeSantis' final months in office and raises questions about dynamics within the administration as the primary election approaches. The situation represents an unusual breach of internal party harmony during what was supposed to be a primary focused on selecting DeSantis' successor.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds raises $90 million in Florida Governor's race as rivals struggle
cards.teaser: U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds has consolidated nearly all major Republican endorsements and raised $90 million for his gubernatorial campaign while his rivals face fundraising and campaign troubles.
cards.body:
U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds has raised $90 million in the Republican gubernatorial race, according to his campaign, with Division of Elections records through June 26 showing nearly $10 million in contributions to his campaign account and more than $76.2 million to the Friends of Byron Donalds political committee. Nearly $2 million was raised between June 20 and June 26, with major contributors including GOPAC Election Fund, Ferreira Construction of New Jersey, Phillips Infrastructure of Tennessee, and the Southern Group. Donalds recently made a $20 million statewide ad buy on television and digital platforms. He has consolidated virtually all meaningful endorsements, securing support from U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody, Attorney General James Uthmeier, Agriculture Secretary Wilton Simpson, CFO Blaise Ingoglia, incoming Florida Senate President Jim Boyd, and Florida House Speaker-designate Sam Garrison.

In contrast, Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins raised nearly $15,500 in hard money and just $100 to his Quiet Professionals FL political committee during the same week, with less than $3.5 million as of June 26. During a Friday night debate with former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner and investment manager James Fishback, Collins struggled with answers on issues ranging from data centers to voting for DeSantis in 2018, which he could not do because he was not a Florida resident yet. Collins also lost his temper at various points and needed notes to help with his responses.

cards.headline: 40-year-old driver killed in head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
cards.body:
A fatal head-on collision claimed the life of a 40-year-old driver early Sunday morning on State Road 710 in Martin County. The crash occurred around 2 a.m. near the intersection of State Road 710, also known as Beeline Highway, and Southwest Silver Fox Lane, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.

The FHP investigation determined that a 2015 Kia Optima traveling north on SR-710 crossed into the southbound lane, directly colliding with a 2021 Toyota Tundra. The front left side of the Kia struck the front left side of the Tundra in the head-on impact. The force of the collision caused the Kia to burst into flames. The vehicle came to rest on the grass shoulder facing north. The Tundra was pushed to a stop facing southeast in the southbound lane.

The 40-year-old driver of the Kia was pronounced dead at the scene. The driver of the Tundra, a 41-year-old man from Indiantown, sustained injuries in the crash. He was transported by Lifestar helicopter from the scene to a medical facility for treatment.

The Florida Highway Patrol is continuing its investigation into the circumstances of the crash. State Road 710 serves as a major north-south route through western Martin County, connecting Indiantown and other communities in the region. This remains a developing story, and additional information may be released as the investigation continues.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Florida students reach 60% proficiency milestone in reading and math
cards.teaser: For the first time in state history, 60% of Florida students tested at or above grade level in both reading and math on the annual Florida Assessment of Student Thinking exam.
cards.body:
For the first time in state history, 60% of Florida students tested at or above grade level in both reading and math on the annual Florida Assessment of Student Thinking (FAST) exam. Just three years ago, roughly half of Florida students read at grade level, making this year's results a meaningful climb in student proficiency.

The improvement coincided with school grade distributions moving up as well. This year, 76% of Florida's 3,428 graded public schools earned an A or B, up from 71% a year ago. The share of schools earning As jumped from 44% to 51%. The milestone comes amid legitimate questions about what is driving the improvement.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce into artistic destination
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain while connecting local and international artists through an artist-in-residency program.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card Body

The Peacock House Art Foundation operates from the historic Crain Estate, preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain who once lived in the private residence. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the entire facility from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. The foundation has made a conscious effort to preserve the estate's original character, with art director Krystal Masters noting the estate remains 90 percent the way it was when the Crains lived there.

The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate including a gazebo shipped from India. The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, bringing in seven originally that grew to over 100. Among the flock is a beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world, and the art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels with no professional experience required.

cards.headline: U.S. men's soccer team faces Belgium in World Cup Round of 16 without suspended forward
cards.teaser: The United States takes the field Monday night against Belgium at Lumen Field in Seattle after earning the program's first knockout stage victory since 2002.
cards.body:
The U.S. men's national team earned the program's first knockout stage victory since 2002 by dispatching Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 on Wednesday night, though the Americans played the final 26 minutes plus stoppage time with 10 men after forward Folarin Balogun was red-carded. Longtime referee Andy Davies acknowledged the decision was wrong, telling ESPN the contact was purely accidental and an unfortunate result from two players challenging for possession in a normal football movement. Coach Mauricio Pochettino said flatly it was never a red card, and the American camp noted that Lionel Messi made a nearly identical challenge against Algeria earlier in the tournament and received nothing.

Balogun, one of the team's top players, will watch Monday from the stands against Belgium at Lumen Field in Seattle. Belgium earned a Round of 16 win over the United States in the 2014 World Cup and has won six consecutive meetings against the U.S., including a 5-2 friendly rout in March, since the inaugural 1930 World Cup when the Americans recorded their lone victory in the head-to-head series. Despite the suspension and historical disadvantage, the U.S. demonstrated resilience by winning Wednesday without Balogun for the final half-hour. The team is well-coached and physically capable, playing at a venue where the home crowd will be as loud as any in the tournament.

hero.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year, survey finds
hero.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
hero.body:
This year's Fourth of July celebrations will cost families more than they spent last year. The American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey shows that preparing a holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, representing a 4% increase from the previous year. The price hike reflects broader inflationary pressures affecting groceries across multiple categories, with some items experiencing more significant jumps than others.

Inflation is the primary driver behind rising cookout expenses. Ground beef prices have climbed 5.5%, while hamburger buns have increased 7.7%. Strawberries faced particularly steep price increases, jumping 12.4% due to damage from a Florida frost. Ice cream prices are also up, rising 5.3% compared to the previous year. These increases across key Fourth of July staples mean families planning traditional cookouts should expect to pay noticeably more at checkout.

However, not all grocery prices have risen this year. Potato prices have declined, offering savings for those planning to serve potato chips or potato salad at their gatherings. Corn prices have shown more volatility throughout the season, though shoppers can find better deals on locally grown corn from the Glades region. These modest price decreases in some categories provide limited relief from the overall upward trend in cookout costs.

Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends several strategies to manage Fourth of July expenses without sacrificing the holiday meal. She emphasizes the importance of shopping strategically by comparing prices across different stores to identify the best deals for items on your grocery list. Woroch also highlights that families can significantly reduce costs by minimizing food waste, which begins with careful meal planning before heading to the store. By taking time to plan meals in advance and shopping with intention, consumers can better control their cookout budgets despite the inflationary environment affecting grocery prices this season.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange at the Florida Turnpike on Midway Road.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at the Florida Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange addresses a significant gap between Turnpike entrances and exits in the city and is designed to accommodate growth over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027.

Resident Erin Scheumeister said the construction has been noticeable but necessary. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Marine Unit rescues two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters are safe after their small motorized boat sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit and the decision to wear life jackets.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1 in the Intracoastal Waterway. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies said they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a statement. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Stuart breast cancer patient and surgeon speak out after insurance denial hours before reconstruction surgery
cards.teaser: A Stuart breast cancer patient and her surgeon are speaking out after Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled, citing a surgical mesh as investigational.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy. Less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considers investigational with insufficient proof it improves health. GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined.

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and believes insurance companies should reconsider their coverage policies. Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after Billington found a mechanism to make it happen. In response to the denial, Anthem stated it regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence but said the mesh does not currently meet standards required for coverage without FDA approval. Clark and Billington are continuing to fight the denial. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction.

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock closes for $3 million renovation to nearly double slip capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be completed by next Fourth of July. The year-long project will nearly double the facility's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips to accommodate both motorized and non-motorized vessels. Funding comes from a state grant and transportation impact fees. The work includes construction of a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform. With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades serve a dual purpose: increasing capacity and preventing storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. "So the year of waiting will be worth it."

During the closure, the city is accommodating businesses that depend on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, initially had concerns about continuing operations during construction. The city found a solution by allowing the company to build a gate at the end of the non-floating section of the downtown Stuart dock, where they can continue boarding passengers. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, acknowledged the dock's current limitations, particularly on weekends when finding available spots becomes challenging. "Modernizing and expanding this back dock is really going to be great for the city but also for us as well," Kuyrkendall said.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with sister Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: Serena Williams withdrew from her Wimbledon doubles match with sister Venus on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week. The 44-year-old lost her singles match 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 to 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday. In an Instagram post, Serena said she was "heartbroken" about the withdrawal but acknowledged that competing again had been meaningful. "I did everything I could but unfortunately my knee just isn't ready to compete," she wrote. The post included images of four syringes showing fluid drained from her knee after her singles match, along with a video of her walking with strapping on her right leg.

The Williams sisters were scheduled to face Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in what was the only first-round doubles match pushed back to give Serena additional recovery time. Venus, 46, competed in the mixed doubles tournament on Friday with Kevin Krawietz but lost in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool. With the U.S. Open approaching, Serena hinted at a potential return, telling followers to "stay tuned to a city near you." The Williams sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon.

cards.headline: Argentina survives Cape Verde scare 3-2 in South Florida World Cup thriller
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and defending World Cup champion Argentina advanced to the Round of 16 after a dramatic extra-time match against underdog Cape Verde before a pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida.
cards.body:
Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday in a World Cup match that went to extra time, with the go-ahead score credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute. Messi scored in the 29th minute for his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal, while Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1. Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored equalizers for Cape Verde that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida.

Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, 40 years old, made 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi. Cape Verde became the smallest country to reach the World Cup knockout round after securing draws against Spain, Uruguay and Saudi Arabia in group play.

Argentina will face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday in the Round of 16. Messi has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbappé in the Golden Boot race, and extended his World Cup scoring streak to eight matches with 12 goals during that span.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state championship after 10-2 season and district title
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football program is targeting a state championship in the 2026 fall season after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district title. Despite their accomplishments, a second-round playoff exit has motivated the team to advance further in the postseason. Head coach Jimmy Robertson credits the program's veteran leadership to a strong senior class, most of whom joined the football program as freshmen from the middle school ranks. According to Robertson, these four-year players have experienced considerable success throughout their high school careers and are positioned to lead the team toward what could be the program's best season yet.

The Scots have intentionally scheduled tougher opponents for the upcoming season as part of a strategic approach to elevate their competitive level and attract new talent. Senior Jack Williams explained that facing stronger competition prepares the team to compete at a higher level. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that while an undefeated regular season would be ideal, playoff performance ultimately defines a successful year. The team's main objective is advancing further in the postseason than they did last season. Senior Edmyer St. Jean described the daily summer workouts as motivation for the season ahead, saying the team looks forward to the grind as they prepare to break program records.

The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

For the first time in state history, 60% of Florida students tested at or above grade level in both reading and math on the annual Florida Assessment of Student Thinking (FAST) exam. Just three years ago, roughly half of Florida students read at grade level, making this year's results a meaningful climb in student proficiency.

The improvement coincided with school grade distributions moving up as well. This year, 76% of Florida's 3,428 graded public schools earned an A or B, up from 71% a year ago. The share of schools earning As jumped from 44% to 51%. The milestone comes amid legitimate questions about what is driving the improvement.

cards.headline: President Trump's 250th anniversary rally overshadows congressional commemoration commission
cards.teaser: Trump held a campaign-style rally on the National Mall as the 250th anniversary of American independence approached, with his face displayed on banners fluttering from federal buildings across Washington.
cards.body:
President Trump's 250th anniversary rally on the National Mall has overshadowed the bipartisan, congressionally authorized commission supposed to coordinate commemorative events. Trump's face appears on banners across federal buildings in the nation's capital, and he plans to return to the National Mall on July Fourth for what he calls a "Trump rally." Since returning to office in January 2025, Trump has nominated one of his personal lawyers to serve as attorney general, ordered the Department of Justice to pursue his political enemies, deployed the U.S. Marines to the nation's second largest city and leveraged the presidency to enrich himself and his family. He has demanded that comedians who mock him be fired, slapped his name on the Kennedy Center, pushed to seize control of elections, filed lawsuits against news organizations whose coverage he disliked and sued his own government seeking $10 billion in taxpayer money.

Trump's actions have led to comparisons with King George III, the British monarch whose rule inspired the American Revolution. When King Charles III visited Trump this year, the official White House X account posted an image of the two men with the caption "TWO KINGS." At the start of his second term, Trump declared he had ended a New York City transportation program and posted: "LONG LIVE THE KING." Trump rejected the comparison, telling CBS' "60 Minutes" earlier this year: "I'm not a king. If I was a king, I wouldn't be dealing with you." Princeton University historian Julian Zelizer said the label fits differently on Trump, noting that the nation is celebrating founding principles rooted in fears of centralized power corruption.

cards.headline: U.S. men's soccer team faces Belgium in World Cup Round of 16 without suspended forward
cards.teaser: The United States takes the field Monday night against Belgium at Lumen Field in Seattle after earning the program's first knockout stage victory since 2002.
cards.body:
The U.S. men's national team earned the program's first knockout stage victory since 2002 by dispatching Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 on Wednesday night, though the Americans played the final 26 minutes plus stoppage time with 10 men after forward Folarin Balogun was red-carded. Longtime referee Andy Davies acknowledged the decision was wrong, telling ESPN the contact was purely accidental and an unfortunate result from two players challenging for possession in a normal football movement. Coach Mauricio Pochettino said flatly it was never a red card, and the American camp noted that Lionel Messi made a nearly identical challenge against Algeria earlier in the tournament and received nothing.

Balogun, one of the team's top players, will watch Monday from the stands against Belgium at Lumen Field in Seattle. Belgium earned a Round of 16 win over the United States in the 2014 World Cup and has won six consecutive meetings against the U.S., including a 5-2 friendly rout in March, since the inaugural 1930 World Cup when the Americans recorded their lone victory in the head-to-head series. Despite the suspension and historical disadvantage, the U.S. demonstrated resilience by winning Wednesday without Balogun for the final half-hour. The team is well-coached and physically capable, playing at a venue where the home crowd will be as loud as any in the tournament.

cards.headline: Americans mark nation's 250th birthday with varied celebrations and subdued optimism
cards.teaser: In interviews across the United States in the days before the Fourth of July, citizens expressed tempered enthusiasm about the nation's semiquincentennial.
cards.body:
Auto technician Joe Fuqua-Bejarano in Topeka, Kansas, said resilience, not politics, makes Americans awesome as a people. "We've just all got to find unity somewhere, whether that's in laughter or perseverance, and keep everybody cool," he said from the fireworks stand where he operates a booming side business. Christina Zhou, a 25-year-old research assistant from Cambridge, Massachusetts, acknowledged there are lots of points of contention but noted "there are still a lot of beautiful things that are happening." She said she tries to focus on things happening locally, which feels more within personal control.

In Mont Vernon, New Hampshire, farmer Mindy Dean, 50, and her family plan to milk their goats Saturday and possibly attend local fireworks, though the 250th celebration has largely passed her by. "We're just happy Americans," she said. "We kinda do our own thing and just enjoy our freedom as Americans." In contrast, 81-year-old retiree Neil Casey from Nashua, New Hampshire, and his friend Maureen Regan from Cambridge are roaming Boston's historical sites, including Paul Revere's house, and attending Fourth of July events. Regan took heart in soccer fans who came for the World Cup, saying "They love everything we have" and urging Americans to "remember how lucky we are."

hero.headline: 40-year-old driver killed in head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
hero.body:
A fatal head-on collision claimed the life of a 40-year-old driver on State Road 710 in Martin County early Sunday morning. The Florida Highway Patrol responded to the crash, which occurred around 2 a.m. near the intersection of State Road 710, also known as Beeline Highway, and Southwest Silver Fox Lane.

According to the Florida Highway Patrol, a 2015 Kia Optima traveling northbound on SR-710 crossed into the southbound lane, striking a 2021 Toyota Tundra head-on. The collision was severe, with the front left section of the Kia making impact with the front left of the Tundra. The force of the crash caused the Kia to catch fire immediately. After coming to rest, the burning Kia ended up on the grass shoulder facing north, while the Tundra rotated to face southeast in the southbound lane.

The driver of the Kia, a 40-year-old man, was pronounced dead at the scene. Emergency responders transported the driver of the Tundra, a 41-year-old man from Indiantown, to a medical facility via Lifestar helicopter. The names of both drivers have not been released by authorities at this time.

The Florida Highway Patrol continues to investigate the circumstances surrounding the crash. Authorities have not yet determined what caused the Kia driver to cross into the opposing lane. The investigation remains ongoing as officials work to establish the full details of the incident.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce into artistic destination with global artist program
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination by preserving the historic Crain Estate and connecting local and international artists. The nonprofit maintains the former home of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who traveled the world nine times and filled their Florida property with distinctive treasures from their journeys. Jaxson Crain, a tile worker by trade, demonstrated his craftsmanship throughout the entire facility from floors and walls to ceilings. The estate remains largely unchanged from the Crains' time there, with the art director Krystal Masters noting it is 90 percent the way it was when they lived there. Notable preserved features include the smoking and bourbon room with its wood paneling, masculine color scheme, and ornate stained glass that leads to a front patio bar. Among the couple's acquisitions was a gazebo shipped from India with intricate peacocks on it. Guided tours of the gardens and architecture are available every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

The Peacock House takes its name from the birds inhabiting the grounds for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced seven peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, and that original flock has grown to over 100 birds. One notable resident is Bob, a 60-year-old peacock recognizable by his distinctive limp who lives in the house and receives daily hand-feedings from his own bowls. The foundation operates an artist-in-residency program offering simple but elegant accommodations and an art lab providing classes for children and adults of all skill levels, including one-on-one instruction in mediums like sculpting and watercolor.

cards.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida Turnpike near St. Lucie
cards.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans traveled over the Fourth of July weekend, with 61.4 million driving. Heavy rain added to congestion on Florida roads including the Turnpike south of Orlando.
cards.body:
A record 72.2 million Americans traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the Independence Day holiday, according to AAA. Of that number, 61.4 million made the trip by car. Friday's wet weather created difficult driving conditions on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando, with driver Ed Budd saying everyone forgets how to drive when it starts raining.

Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA. Driver Carlos Borras reported smooth sailing on his round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday, seeing no traffic or accidents. However, driver Fernando Amado described a much busier experience, saying Saturday was the day when people were really heading up north.

AAA recommends travelers hit the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion. The heaviest traffic was expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday, and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.
